A member of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Jaitley served as the Minister of Finance "Ministry of Finance (India)") and Corporate Affairs "Minister of Corporate Affairs (India)") of the Government of India from 2014 to 2019. Jaitley previously held the cabinet portfolios of Finance "Minister of Finance (India)"), Defence "Minister of Defence (India)"), Corporate Affairs, Commerce and Industry "Minister of Commerce and Industry (India)"), and Law and Justice "Minister of Law and Justice (India)") in the Vajpayee government and Narendra Modi government. english_retrieval.title: Arun Jaitley | Biography, History, & Facts
english_retrieval.snippet: A leader in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he served as leader of the BJP in the Rajya Sabha (upper chamber of the Indian parliament) from 2009 to 2014. In 2014, he joined Prime Minister Narendra Modi's cabinet. In the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance government (1999–2004), he served in ministerial posts, including minister of Law, Justice, and Company Affairs and minister of Commerce and Industry. He was the leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the Rajya Sabha from 2009 to 2014. Furthermore, Jaitley served as Minister of Law, Justice, and Company Affairs, as well as Minister of Commerce and Industry, in the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance coalition government from 1999 to 2004. In the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition government from 1999 to 2004, he served as Minister of Law, Justice, and Company Affairs and Minister of Commerce and Industry. Jaitley was a key leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and a Rajya Sabha member.
